subject: Clarify BYOK + operator access for private deployment (jurisdiction & telemetry)
body:
Message 1/5
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthco.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: BYOK custody + operator access (jurisdiction questions)

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple follow-ups from our security and legal teams as we evaluate Redwood Private for a European region deployment:

- We need clarity on the default key custody model for Private (VPC / on-prem). Can Redwood operate an HSM in our VPC, or do we need to supply a KMS in our AWS account?
- For customer-controlled keys (BYOK), what exactly can Redwood operators see in telemetry/metrics? Do token traces, prompt/response snippets, or KV cache identifiers ever leave the customer-controlled environment?
- Jurisdiction: if we host in eu-west-1 under our infra, can Redwood confirm that operator access requests (breakglass, maintenance) are handled from EU-based personnel only, and whether any cross-border subprocessors are involved?
- Please attach current subprocessors list and the latest DPA redline we should expect. Our legal wants to start a mark-up pass.

Appreciate a clear, point-by-point response we can share with SecOps and Legal.

Best,
Sara
Head of Security Operations
HealthCo

---

Message 2/5
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthco.com>
Cc: HealthCo Legal <legal@healthco.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK custody + operator access (jurisdiction questions)

Sara — thanks, great questions. Quick summary up front, and I attached two files: a current DPA redline (PDF stub) and our subprocessors snapshot (CSV stub). Long answers below.

Short answers (TL;DR):
1) BYOK options: we support both models: (A) customer-managed KMS in your cloud account (recommended for full key custody), or (B) Redwood-managed HSM provisioned into your VPC under a customer-controlled project with CMKs derived under your tenant (less common). Either approach supports crypto separation; option A gives you strongest legal control.

2) Telemetry & operator observability: With BYOK option A (customer KMS), plaintexts/response payloads do not leave your encrypted storage or network unless you configure export. Our runtime still collects operational metrics (latency, token counts, anonymized error traces). We never collect prompt/response text in persistent telemetry when BYOK is enabled; ephemeral traces used for debugging are truncated and require explicit opt-in and documented breakglass.

3) Jurisdiction & access: For EU-region Private deployments hosted in your AWS account, routine operator access is performed via an access broker into your VPC and is restricted per policy. We can agree contractually to EU-based operator time-zone restrictions for breakglass escalation, and we support privileged access requests that require 2-person approval and an auditable ticket with session recording. We will provide the subprocessors CSV for transparency; critical subprocessors (monitoring, backup, build tooling) are listed.

4) DPA and redlines: attached is our starting DPA redline. We are open to narrowing subprocessors scope, adding strict data transfer clauses, and adding obligations for operator locality for this account.

Long form details:
- BYOK technical patterns:
  • Customer KMS (recommended): You create and manage the CMK in your cloud provider. Redwood obtains per-request data keys that are encrypted with the CMK; we never hold the unwrapped CMK. Persistent artifacts (model weights, cached keys) remain encrypted under customer-controlled envelopes.
  • Redwood-managed keystore in your VPC: we can deploy a FIPS-certified HSM appliance in your VPC project and wrap keys under tenant-specific KEKs. Keys are accessible to runtime nodes but are never exported as plaintext outside the VPC. This option requires an operations onboarding window.

- Telemetry clarity:
  • Metrics: token counts, RPC latencies, error categories (aggregated) — always allowed.
  • Debug traces: isolated to ephemeral sessions, redacted by default, only captured when you approve a session (breakglass) and with recording stored in your account.
  • KV cache identifiers: hashed and salted identifiers may be present in logs for cache hits; they are opaque and not reversible.

- Operator access & breakglass
  • We can contractually require EU-only operator handling for your account under the dedicated access SLA.
  • All operator sessions are ticketed, 2-person approved, time-limited, and recorded.

I'd like to set up a 30-minute call with your SecOps + Legal to walk the DPA redline. Grace and Marcus on our side are engineers who can cover HSM provisioning and operator controls.

Attachments: redline_dpa_healthco_v1.pdf (redline stub), subprocessors_snapshot_20260829.csv

Regards,
Elliot Price
Senior Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

---

Message 3/5 (internal planning)
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: BYOK custody + operator access (HealthCo)

Folks — forwarding HealthCo questions (see thread). They'd like EU-only operator handling and confirmation about BYOK behavior. Can you review the CSV and confirm: (1) whether our monitoring subprocessor (CloudProbe Inc.) stores any request bodies in any EU region snapshots, and (2) whether we can operationalize EU-only operator allowlist for this account?

Key asks for call: HSM provisioning lead times, required network peering, and changes to runbook for session recording retention.

Thanks — Elliot

---

Message 4/5
From: HealthCo Legal <legal@healthco.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthco.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK custody + operator access (jurisdiction questions)

Elliot,

Appreciate the quick reply. A few legal redlines we'd like to propose after an initial scan of the attached DPA:
1) Narrow subprocessors to the EU-only list for our account, or require explicit prior written consent for any non-EU subprocessor.
2) Add clause: operator access to customer environment must be performed only by personnel physically located in the EU and subject to EU employment contracts.
3) Stronger data transfer protections for telemetry — explicitly forbid export of any request/response content to third countries; allow only aggregated metrics outside EU.

We'd like to markup and return the DPA. Where should we upload the redlined PDF? Also please confirm whether CloudProbe Inc. supports on-prem agent mode (they are listed as a subprocessor).

Legal will be on the call Monday.

Regards,
HealthCo Legal

Attachment referenced: proposed_markups_inbox (we will upload)

---

Message 5/5
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: HealthCo Legal <legal@healthco.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthco.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Darren Liu <darren.liu@auditfirm.io>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK custody + operator access (jurisdiction questions)

Thanks — quick operational updates before the call: 

- Subprocessors: CloudProbe Inc. confirmed they have an EU agent/collector mode; we can configure their agent to run within your VPC and keep raw logs in your account. I asked for a stamped attestation and attached the subprocessors CSV we maintain.
- Operator locality: we can include a contractual addendum to require EU-resident operator handling for this tenant. For full legal parity (EU employment contracts), we'd need a scoped exception and can propose language that restricts operator accounts to our EU SRE team for this customer.
- Telemetry: we will add a prohibition on exporting request/response content outside EU when BYOK is selected and include an explicit aggregated metrics carve-out.

Next steps:
1) Please upload your DPA markups to this shared folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/privdep/design-specs/healthco-onprem-plan (we prefer a single PDF).
2) I'd like to schedule a 30-min call Monday 2026-08-31 09:00 CEST / 00:00 PDT — does that work for your team?
3) Internal: Grace and Marcus will prepare a short runbook for HSM provisioning (networking, peering, keys lifecyle) and a sample session recording retention policy.

I'd also be happy to loop in our compliance partner (Darren Liu) for a pre-call attestation. CC him.

Attachments: subprocessors_snapshot_20260829.csv (latest export)

Regards,
Elliot Price
Senior Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
